Amelia — thanks for the note and the redlines. Attaching Redwood's current DPA (v3) and our maintained subprocessor list.

Quick summary: we can accept most of Paywise's language but there are two items that need privacy/security review and an exception path:
1) Paywise added a carve-out requiring HSM-backed key custody for all customer data at rest. Our standard is customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and platform-managed KMS for hosted; HSM-only for certain enterprise customers is an exception.
2) The analytics vendor called out in your redlines performs EU->US transfers under our standard SCC+contractual safeguards, but the proposed added audit frequency and explicit subprocess erasure clause are nonstandard and will need sign-off.

I’ve flagged both for Neha (Privacy) and Priyom (Sales Ops/legal coordination). We’ll aim to respond fast but we may need an approved exception for the HSM ask or some compensating controls. Can you confirm the procurement deadline (time zone) so we can prioritize?

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.docx, Subprocessor_List_202705.csv

Best,
Lauren Bishop

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Paywise DPA redlines — need exception & evidence (procurement deadline 7/16 COB)

Lauren / Priyom — thanks for the heads up and the materials. Quick privacy/security read:
- The analytics subprocessor relies on SCC+contract controls; that is acceptable in principle. However, the requested accelerated audit cadence and mandatory erasure on 30 days are operationally risky. We should propose: (a) documented retention policy with data minimization scope + (b) quarterly attestation from the subprocessor and on-demand audit rights limited to verified incidents.
- For the HSM ask: that is a high bar and not standard for hosted customers. We can entertain an exception limited to the Paywise account if they accept: (i) customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys OR (ii) platform-managed KMS with annual HSM attestation + constrained access controls.

Evidence checklist to close quickly:
1) SOC 2 Type II report covering relevant controls (latest report).
2) Subprocessor architecture note showing where EU data resides and transfer mechanism.
3) Confirmation of encryption-in-transit and at-rest (TLS + AES-256) and whether keys are HSM-backed.

If we can get those three items within 24 hours, I am comfortable approving a scoped exception. Marcus — if privacy and security are comfortable, please provide an official exception paragraph that we can attach to the envelope. Otherwise we risk delaying procurement to Monday.

-Neha
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Black <amelia.black@paywise.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Paywise DPA redlines — Exec approval for scoped exception

Amelia / Paywise procurement,

Thanks for your patience. We’ve reviewed the Paywise redlines and, subject to the mitigations below, Redwood is prepared to accept a scoped exception to our standard DPA to accommodate Paywise’s requirements. Conditions (to be included as a one-paragraph addendum attached to the DocuSign envelope):
1) Exception scope: applies only to the Paywise account (Deal ID: PW-2027-0491) and the named analytics subprocessor listed in our Subprocessor_List_202705.csv.
2) Required evidence to be provided within 48 hours of signature: a current SOC 2 Type II for the subprocessor, a short architecture note confirming EU data handling and transfer mechanism, and confirmation that encryption in-transit and at-rest (AES-256) is in place. If keys are platform-managed, annual HSM attestation is acceptable.
3) Retention and erasure: Paywise and Redwood will agree to a retention schedule; the subprocessor will provide quarterly attestations and on-demand audit rights in case of suspected incidents (not blanket monthly erasure).
4) Remedy: any deviation from the above will trigger a remediation plan and potential suspension of subprocessing activities.

Assuming Paywise accepts the paragraph, Redwood is happy to sign via DocuSign and proceed with onboarding. Please confirm acceptance so we can finalize the envelope.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer & Legal Ops
Redwood Inference
